workstream: W4 — The Retention Meta (daily board, forgiving streak, shape collection, share artifact, notifications, store review) — and the persistence widening that all of it depends on
goal: A player who opens Arrows tomorrow has a reason that is not "level N+1": one date-seeded board that is the same for everyone that day, a day streak that is visible and survives one missed day, a gallery of the 26 silhouettes they have actually drawn, and a text card they can paste into a chat — all stored in a versioned save file that upgrades an existing install without losing a single solved level.
non_goals: ENERGY / LIVES GATING — rejected. PRODUCT.md's session is 'commute, couch, before bed' and 'no timers, no pressure'; an energy meter is a timer wearing a different hat and would make the calm positioning a lie. It also has no evidence behind it here: the retention lever with a real controlled result in this genre is difficulty matching (Li et al., KDD 2021, n=29,302), not artificial scarcity.

PAID STREAK FREEZES — rejected as a SKU, adopted as a free mechanic (W4-06). Duolingo's evidence is about the freeze CAP (1 -> 2-3) raising returns, not about selling them. Selling forgiveness converts the one mechanic whose evidence is 'be kinder' into a pressure surface, and Block Blast (~15M DAU, ~$1M/day on ads, ~$66k lifetime IAP) is evidence that a small IAP ladder is not where this game's money is.

LEAGUES / PvP LEADERBOARDS — rejected. They need a server, an account, a moderation surface and anti-cheat; the daily board here is client-seeded off the device clock and therefore trivially forgeable. NYT Games runs 11.2B plays/year on self-competition only (streaks, personal bests) with no ladder, which is the proof that the ladder is optional. Also directly contradicts 'calm, night, minimal'.

COIN CURRENCY WITH A HINT SHOP — rejected. Hints are already rewarded-ad-gated (GameScreen.tsx onHint), which is the one ad format positively associated with retention. Inserting a currency between the player and the hint adds a wallet, a shop screen, a balance HUD and a pricing problem, and violates 'flow over menus'.

SEASONAL / FOMO EVENTS — rejected. They need remote config and live-ops content the project has neither the tooling nor the staffing for (no remote config, no analytics, no crash reporting), and the incumbent (Lessmore/Miniclip, 100M+ installs) runs weekly themes and monthly challenges at a cadence a solo dev cannot match. Competing on live-ops is the one axis where losing is guaranteed.

LEVEL-SELECT GRID — rejected. Named explicitly in PRODUCT.md's anti-references ('cluttered level-select grids and menus the player navigates every session') and contradicted by design principle 3 ('flow over menus'). The shape gallery in W4-07 is deliberately NOT navigable into play for exactly this reason.

PERSISTING THE INTERSTITIAL COUNTER. src/ui/ads.tsx:255 `let finishedGames = 0` is an in-memory module variable that resets on cold start; that is a real monetisation bug but it belongs to the monetisation workstream, not here. W4-01 leaves room for it: if it is later persisted it MUST be added to SaveSystem.persistenceKeys or it will silently never hydrate.

iOS. The native board view has not compiled since 2026-09-01 (docs/IOS_BOARD_PLAN.md) and there is no ATT / SKAdNetwork configuration. Every step here is specified and verified on Android; the iOS notification and store-review paths are written but explicitly not verified.

steps.title: Versioned save schema: add a schema-version key and 11 new int keys, with a non-destructive v0->v1 migration
steps.what:
In src/core/saveSystem.ts: add `const SchemaKey = 'arrows_schema_version'` plus eleven new keys and append them to the frozen `PersistenceKeys` array at lines 41-50 (order: existing eight first, new ones appended — never reordered, because storage.test.ts asserts the array by value). New keys, all int, all defaulting to 0: `arrows_schema_version`, `arrows_daily_day`, `arrows_daily_streak`, `arrows_daily_best`, `arrows_streak_shields`, `arrows_shapes_seen_lo`, `arrows_shapes_seen_hi`, `arrows_notif_optin` (0 = never asked, 1 = granted, 2 = declined), `arrows_notif_hour`, `arrows_review_last_day`, `arrows_review_count`. Add `SaveSystem.SCHEMA_VERSION = 1` and a `migrate()` called once from `initSaveSystem()` in src/ui/storage.ts AFTER `store.hydrate()` and AFTER `SaveSystem.useStore(store)`: if the stored version is < 1 it writes only `arrows_schema_version = 1` and touches nothing else. Add `SaveSystem.useClock(fn: () => Date)` (default `() => new Date()`) and route `dayNumber` (saveSystem.ts:56-60) through it, so every day-boundary rule in W4-03/05/06/09/10 is testable without fake timers leaking into unrelated suites.

STORE WIDENING — the explicit answer: the IntStore interface (getInt/setInt/deleteKey, saveSystem.ts:12-16) is NOT widened, because every W4 field packs into an int. The shape collection is a bitmask split across two 30-bit keys (`_lo` = catalog indices 0-29, `_hi` = 30-59), giving 60 shapes of headroom against the 26 that exist today (measured: exactly 26 distinct shape names across levels 0-599, see W4-02). Day numbers are small ints (2026-09-09 = 2443 under the existing 2020-01-01 local epoch), streaks and counters are small ints, the notification hour is 0-23. The ONE thing that would force a widening is a per-level or per-day history (e.g. 'which board did I play on 2026-04-11'), and that is not in this workstream; if it is ever wanted, widen by adding `getString/setString` to IntStore and a matching branch in HydratedIntStore, and bump SCHEMA_VERSION to 2 — do not smuggle strings through getInt.

WIPE-RISK ANALYSIS. (a) The hydrate path reads exactly `SaveSystem.persistenceKeys` (storage.ts:20). A key that is written but absent from that array reads its default forever after a cold start while its writes still land on disk — the 'works until you kill the app' failure. Adding the key to the frozen array is therefore not bookkeeping, it is the feature. (b) The migration must never call `AsyncStorage.clear()`, `getAllKeys()`, `multiRemove` or `SaveSystem.resetProgress()` (saveSystem.ts:146-153). storage.test.ts:46 already asserts getAllKeys is never called; keep that assertion and add the same for multiRemove during migration. (c) There is no checksum or signature over the save, so an additive key cannot invalidate the rest — the class of bug that wipes saves via a checksum gate does not exist here, and must not be introduced. (d) Downgrade: a player on the W4 build who sideloads versionCode 6 hydrates only the eight legacy keys; the eleven new ones sit untouched on disk and rehydrate on the next W4 launch. No destructive path. (e) Android Auto Backup is already ON (allowBackup="true", no dataExtractionRules), so these keys will silently start being backed up and restored across devices — a restored save may carry a `arrows_daily_day` from the future relative to the new device's clock, which W4-05 must tolerate (treat `storedDay > today` as 'not played today' rather than negative arithmetic).
steps.why: Audit finding: SaveSystem is 8 frozen int keys with no schema version, so 'a collection, a daily record or a per-level history cannot be stored today'. Every other step in W4 writes state. This is also the step where the project's own scar applies — persisted-schema changes without a migration + wipe-risk note are a standing red flag, and the frozen-array-plus-hydrate contract means a forgotten key fails silently rather than loudly.
acceptance: `SaveSystem.persistenceKeys` has exactly 19 entries, is still `Object.isFrozen`, and its first eight entries are byte-identical to the current list in storage.test.ts:36-45 in the same order.

One `AsyncStorage.multiGet` call at boot, with all 19 keys, and `AsyncStorage.getAllKeys` never called (both already asserted at storage.test.ts:33 and :46 — the assertions must be updated for the new length, not deleted).

Simulated upgrade: with the AsyncStorage mock seeded with ONLY the eight legacy keys at non-default values (current_level=37, total_solved=412, perfect_streak=5, best_perfect_streak=9, day_streak=4, last_play_day=2440, sound_on=0, dark_mode=1), after `initSaveSystem()` every legacy getter returns exactly the seeded value, `arrows_schema_version` reads 1, and `AsyncStorage.multiRemove` was never called.
Fresh install: version reads 1 after boot; all eleven new keys read 0; `currentLevel` reads 0.
Re-running `initSaveSystem()` on an already-v1 store performs no writes at all (multiSet not called).
`SaveSystem.useClock` is honoured by `dayNumber`: injecting a fixed Date makes `dayStreak` deterministic without touching global timers.
steps.verification: (1) `npx jest src/ui/__tests__/storage.test.ts` with the new upgrade case above — this exercises the original failing path because the bug being prevented is 'a key outside persistenceKeys never hydrates', and the test asserts the hydrate call's key list AND reads every legacy value back after a simulated upgrade. (2) DEVICE, and this one is mandatory because the jest mock is not AsyncStorage: on the API 31 emulator install the current shipping build (versionCode 6), play to level 4 and toggle Ink Night on, then `adb install -r` the W4 build over it WITHOUT uninstalling, cold-start it, and screenshot the menu. Pass = wordmark screen reads 'Level 4' in Ink Night. This exercises the real on-disk AsyncStorage SQLite file that the unit test replaces with a mock, which is where a migration actually breaks. (3) Downgrade check: `adb install -r --downgrade` back to versionCode 6, screenshot the menu (must still read Level 4), then reinstall W4 and confirm the daily/collection keys still read their pre-downgrade values.
steps.risk: HIGH BLAST RADIUS, LOW LIKELIHOOD. The failure mode is losing existing players' progress, which is unrecoverable and invisible in code review. Mitigations: the migration is additive-only (one write of one key) and there is no code path in it that deletes; the test suite asserts multiRemove is never called during boot. NOT flag-gated on purpose — a feature flag around a schema migration creates two on-disk shapes and doubles the migration matrix. Rollback is the versionCode-6 downgrade path verified in step (3): the old build ignores the new keys entirely. Second risk: appending to a frozen array that a test asserts by value means a careless later edit reorders it and silently reinterprets `arrows_shapes_seen_lo` bit positions — W4-02's order-lock test is the guard.
steps.brand_perf_check: FLAG TEST: not applicable — no motion, no animated node, nothing drawn. Zero arrows animated, zero new Skia nodes, static layer untouched. Boot cost: one multiGet grows from 8 to 19 keys (a single native round-trip either way) plus at most one extra multiSet on the first upgrade launch. Brand gates: none engaged (no UI).

steps.title: Freeze a canonical 26-shape catalog and add a cheap shape-name lookup (1480x faster than full generation)
steps.what:
In src/core/shapeLibrary.ts add `Catalog: readonly ShapeDef[]` — one frozen, explicitly ordered array of all 26 shapes — alongside the existing SimplePool/MediumPool/ComplexPool (lines 281-291). The pools overlap (Circle and Diamond appear in both SimplePool and MediumPool), so there is no existing array that enumerates the set; I verified the union is exactly 26 by generating levels 0-599 and collecting distinct `shapeName` (Arrow, Bolt, Butterfly, Cat, Circle, Crescent, Crown, Diamond, Fish, Flower, Heart, Hexagon, Hourglass, Mushroom, Octagon, Pentagon, Pine, Plus, Rectangle, Ring, Rocket, Square, Star, Triangle, Trophy, X). Add `ShapeLibrary.catalogIndexOf(name: string): number` returning -1 for unknown.

In src/core/levelGenerator.ts export `shapeNameFor(levelIndex: number): string` = `ShapeLibrary.pick(Difficulties.forLevel(i), new DotNetRandom(seed(i))).name`. This is exact, not an approximation: `generate()` (lines 44-49) constructs the rng and calls `pick` as the FIRST consumption of that rng, before `targetCells`, so the shape is fully determined before any expensive work. Do not change `seed()` (levelGenerator.ts:382-384) or the order of rng draws in `generate()` — every existing player's level N must stay byte-identical.

Export `Catalog` and `shapeNameFor` from src/core/index.ts.
steps.why: Two later steps need this. The collection (W4-07) persists a shape as a BIT POSITION, so the catalog order becomes part of the save format and must be frozen and tested — reordering it silently rewrites what every player has collected. And the collection backfill for existing players needs the shape of levels 0..currentLevel-1, which via full generation is far too slow (measured below) and via `shapeNameFor` is free.
acceptance: `ShapeLibrary.Catalog.length === 26`, all names distinct, `Object.isFrozen` true, and every member of SimplePool, MediumPool and ComplexPool appears in it.

ORDER LOCK: a test asserts the exact 26-name array in order, with a comment stating that the index is persisted as a bit position and reordering breaks saves. Appending is allowed; inserting or reordering must fail the test.

`shapeNameFor(i) === LevelGenerator.generate(i).shapeName` for every i in 0..999. MEASURED: 0 mismatches (script: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gentlegen-Desktop-Projects-arrows-game/529758e6-3b29-4422-a19a-51e6c72a0675/scratchpad/m3.ts, to be committed as scripts/analysis/shape-lookup-equivalence.ts).

`shapeNameFor` costs under 5 ms for 1000 levels on the dev machine. MEASURED on this Mac, Node 20: 2.17 ms per 1000 calls, vs 3211.6 ms per 1000 `LevelGenerator.generate` calls — a ~1480x reduction (same script family, m2.ts/m3.ts).
`LevelGenerator.generate(0)`, `generate(1)`, `generate(167)` produce identical arrowCount/shapeName/board serialization to the pre-change build (regression guard on the untouched seed path).
steps.verification: `npx jest src/core/__tests__/levelGenerator.test.ts` with the equivalence loop over levels 0..999 and the order-lock assertion. This exercises the thing being changed because the risk is precisely that a cheap lookup diverges from the real generator on some level — so the test compares the two implementations across a thousand real levels rather than asserting the lookup against itself. The 1480x number is reproducible by running the committed scripts/analysis script and reading its printed timings; the timings are dev-machine numbers on Node, NOT Hermes-on-device, and the acceptance criterion is deliberately the correctness equivalence, not the timing.
steps.risk: Low, with one sharp edge: any future edit that inserts a shape into the middle of Catalog, or that adds an rng draw before `ShapeLibrary.pick` inside `generate()`, breaks either saved collections or the equivalence. Both are covered by the two tests above. Rollback: pure addition, revert the commit. No flag needed.
steps.brand_perf_check: FLAG TEST: not applicable — no motion, no animated node, no Skia node, static layer untouched. Runtime cost is zero on the gameplay path (nothing calls it during play). Brand gates: none engaged.

steps.title: Date-seeded daily board generator, in its own seed namespace, drawing from all 26 shapes
steps.what:
In src/core/levelGenerator.ts add `generateDaily(dayNumber: number): GeneratedLevel` — the same pipeline as `generate()` but with three deliberate differences.

(1) SEED NAMESPACE. `generate()` uses `seed(i) = Math.imul((2166136261 ^ i)|0, 16777619)|0` (line 383). Reusing it with the day number would hand a campaign player the identical board: today, 2026-09-09, is day 2443 under the existing epoch (saveSystem.ts:56-60), and level 2443 is a level a real player can reach. Use a two-round FNV with a namespace byte instead: `dailySeed(d) { let h = 2166136261; h = Math.imul(h ^ 0x64, 16777619); h = Math.imul(h ^ d, 16777619); return h|0; }`. MEASURED: 0 collisions between `dailySeed(d)` for d in 0..19999 (~54 years) and `seed(i)` for i in 0..199999; reusing `seed(day)` collides on 20000 of 20000 days by construction (script m3.ts).

(2) SHAPE POOL. Draw from `ShapeLibrary.Catalog` (all 26) rather than `ShapeLibrary.pick`, whose Normal pool is only Square/Rectangle/Circle/Diamond (shapeLibrary.ts:281, 302-308). MEASURED over 3650 days: each shape appears 135-146 times against an expected 140 — near-uniform; and consecutive-day shape repeats are 4 out of 3649, far below the ~140 chance expectation, i.e. the day-to-day board visibly changes shape (script m4.ts). Note honestly that this low repeat rate is a property of DotNetRandom's first draw across adjacent seeds, not a designed guarantee — the acceptance test asserts the measured distribution rather than assuming it.

(3) SIZE BAND. Use `Difficulties.config(Difficulty.Normal)` (difficulty.ts:63-65, cells 260-400) for every daily, regardless of the 6-level cycle. MEASURED daily arrow counts over 3650 days with this configuration: min 45, p10 64, median 82, p90 100, max 145, mean 82.1 — statistically the same band as campaign Normal levels (median 83, p25 73, p75 93, n=400 over levels 0-599, script m.ts).

Core-only step: no UI, no persistence, no screen. `generateDaily` returns the same `GeneratedLevel` shape the existing GameScreen already consumes.
steps.why: Audit finding: Arrows has no daily content and every serious competitor ships one; the generator is already deterministic so date-seeding is nearly free. Naavik's constraint — the daily must be completable in a NEW player's first session — is why the daily is pinned to the smallest measured band rather than following the difficulty cycle (which would serve a 224-arrow SuperHard board on some days). Drawing from all 26 shapes answers the separate audit finding that 4 shapes are 71% of levels and 33% of levels are a plain rectangle: the daily is the one board every player sees, so it is the worst possible place to show a plain filled rectangle a third of the time.
acceptance: Determinism: `generateDaily(d)` called twice returns identical arrowCount, shapeName, rows, cols and board serialization, for d = 0, 2443, 9999.
Namespace separation: `dailySeed(d) !== seed(i)` for all d in 0..19999 and i in 0..199999 (measured: 0 collisions).
Size band over days 0..3649: median arrow count within 75-90 and p90 <= 105 (measured: median 82, p90 100). These bounds are the measured distribution +/- headroom, not invented targets.
Shape spread over days 0..3649: all 26 shapes appear; no shape appears more than 160 or fewer than 120 times (measured range 135-146); consecutive-day identical shapes <= 20 of 3649 (measured 4).

Solvability: 30 random-greedy playthroughs across 30 different day numbers each clear in exactly arrowCount taps with zero dead ends (the same harness that proved the campaign boards are never brickable).
The campaign path is untouched: `generate(i)` output for i = 0, 1, 5, 167 is byte-identical to the pre-change build.
steps.verification: `npx jest src/core/__tests__/levelGenerator.test.ts` for determinism, namespace separation, the campaign regression and the greedy-solvability sweep; plus `npx tsx scripts/analysis/daily-band.ts` (the committed version of scratchpad m4.ts) printing the distribution table that the band assertions are derived from. This exercises the change rather than restating it, because the specific hazards are (a) a daily colliding with a campaign level and (b) a daily landing on a 224-arrow board — and both are asserted over the full 54-year day range and the full 3650-day distribution rather than on a single sample day.
steps.risk: Low; it is additive core code with no callers until W4-05. The one real risk is the seed namespace: if `seed()` is ever changed, the collision measurement is void — the test re-derives it from both live functions rather than hardcoding, so it fails loudly. Rollback: unused code until W4-05 wires it, so reverting is free.
steps.brand_perf_check: FLAG TEST: not applicable — no motion, no animated node, no change to the static layer or the 2-trail / 4-Skia-node ceilings. Cost: one extra board generation, on demand, only when the player opens the daily — the same cost the app already pays per level. Brand gates: respects 'no timers' (a daily board is not a timed board), and does not introduce a level-select grid.

steps.title: Measure time-to-clear before claiming the daily is first-session completable
steps.what:
Add a dev-only instrumentation path in src/ui/GameScreen.tsx (behind `__DEV__` plus an `EXPO_PUBLIC_MEASURE_CLEAR=1` env gate, in the same style as src/perfMode.ts) that records, per level: level index or day number, shape name, arrow count, ms from first tap to clear, tap count, and hearts lost — logged to console in one line and nothing else. Then run a human playtest: the owner (or a recruited player) plays 8 daily boards drawn from days spanning the measured band (2 near p10 = 64 arrows, 4 near the median = 82, 2 near p90 = 100) on the API 31 emulator or a phone, cold, without hints. Record the median and range of time-to-clear and of taps-per-clear.

Deliverable: a committed docs/daily-time-to-clear-<date>.md with the raw rows, the median, the sample size and the explicit caveat that n is small and the players are not new players.

Explicitly NOT the method: an automated 'tap every currently-clearable arrow' harness. It would measure the mechanical floor, and the audit already established that no order can brick a board and the real game is a visual-search / attention task — so an automated sweep measures the one thing that is not the difficulty.
steps.why: Naavik's requirement for a daily is 'completable in a new player's FIRST session', and W4-05's design (one board, no save-and-resume mid-daily) rests on it. There is no analytics, no crash reporting and no session-length data in this app, so the claim is currently unmeasurable from the product. The project's standing rule is that a brief pinning a number must name the measurement that produced it; this step is that measurement, and it is a step rather than a footnote because W4-05 cannot honestly claim first-session completability without it.
acceptance: A committed markdown file containing at least 8 rows (day number, shape, arrow count, taps, ms, hearts lost), a median, a min/max, the device and build used, and a stated sample-size caveat.
The instrumentation compiles out of a release build: `EXPO_PUBLIC_MEASURE_CLEAR` unset produces no logging call site reachable at runtime (same inlining contract as PERF_MODE in src/perfMode.ts).

A written verdict line: either 'median time-to-clear <= X min, daily band confirmed' or 'median exceeds X, W4-03's daily band must be re-tuned downward and W4-03's acceptance bounds re-derived'. X is the owner's call (see escalation), not a number this brief invents.
steps.verification: Read the committed markdown and reproduce one row: run the instrumented build on the emulator with a fixed day number, play that board to clear, and confirm the logged arrow count matches `generateDaily(d).arrowCount` and the logged tap count equals the arrow count plus mistakes. This checks the instrument itself before any decision is aimed at its output — the project has been burned by percentiles quoted over unreconciled sample counts, so the row-level reconciliation (taps = arrows + mistakes) is the reconciliation.
steps.risk: The measurement is 8 sessions by non-new players — it bounds the mechanical time honestly but cannot measure a genuine first-timer's search time. It must be labelled that way wherever the number is used, and it must NOT be quoted as a retention figure. Rollback: env-gated dev code, delete or leave inert.
steps.brand_perf_check: FLAG TEST: not applicable — logging only, no motion, no animated node, no Skia node, static layer untouched. The log call fires once per clear, not per tap, so it cannot land inside the per-tap frame budget. Brand gates: none engaged (no shipped UI).

steps.title: Daily board entry, its own streak, and one-per-day completion state
steps.what:
MENU: add a second, quieter action beneath the Play pill in src/ui/HomeScreen.tsx — a text button reading 'Today's board' (undone) or 'Today's board · done' (done), in `inkDim`, not a second violet pill (there is exactly one primary action per PRODUCT.md's 'one violet accent'). Below it, the daily streak line from W4-06.

SCREEN: reuse `GameScreen` with a new optional prop `daily?: { day: number }`. When set, the session is built from `LevelGenerator.generateDaily(day)` instead of `createLevelSession` (src/ui/gameSessionLifecycle.ts:17-23 gains a `createDailySession(day, revision)` sibling), the header's 'LEVEL N' label reads the date instead, and the win panel's 'Next level' button becomes 'Done' returning to the menu — a daily must not roll into level N+1.

PERSISTENCE (keys from W4-01): on a daily clear call a new `SaveSystem.registerDailySolve()` which, using the injected clock, sets `arrows_daily_day = today`, extends `arrows_daily_streak` if the stored day was exactly yesterday, restarts it at 1 otherwise, and raises `arrows_daily_best`. It must NOT touch `arrows_current_level` — the daily never advances campaign progress. It SHOULD call the existing `SaveSystem.registerSolve(perfect)` so the daily counts toward totalSolved, the perfect streak and the calendar-day streak (the daily is a solve; making it not count would punish the player for choosing it).

RULES: one attempt outcome per day. Losing all hearts on the daily shows the existing lose panel with Retry (the board is regenerated identically from the same day — deterministic), so the daily is forgiving, not one-shot. Completion is recorded only on a clear. A player who has already cleared today can re-enter and replay it (the button reads 'done'), but `registerDailySolve` is a no-op when `arrows_daily_day === today`.

CLOCK EDGE CASES, all decided explicitly: the day boundary is local midnight via the existing `dayNumber` (saveSystem.ts:56-60), the same function the calendar streak uses, so 'today' never disagrees between the two features. A restored Auto Backup save (or a rolled-back device clock) can leave `arrows_daily_day > today`: treat that as 'not played today' and simply overwrite on the next clear — never compute a negative gap. Changing the device clock yields a different daily; there is no server and nothing competitive at stake (leaderboards are rejected), so this is accepted, not defended against.

Flag: `DAILY_ENABLED` constant, default ON at release but present so the menu entry and the daily route can be disabled in one edit if the board proves too long.
steps.why: The daily is the load-bearing retention system this genre runs on and the product has none; the generator makes it nearly free. It is placed as a secondary, quiet entry rather than a competing primary because PRODUCT.md's design principle 3 is 'flow over menus' — the default path must stay Open -> Play -> resume.
acceptance: Two devices (or two emulator profiles) with the same local date open the daily and see the same shape name and the same arrow count in the header.
Clearing the daily does not change the campaign resume level: menu reads 'Level N' before and after, verified by screenshot pairs.
Clearing the daily increments `totalSolved` and the calendar `dayStreak` exactly as a campaign clear does (unit test on SaveSystem with an injected clock).

`arrows_daily_streak` extends only across consecutive local days: injected-clock test covering same-day repeat (no change), yesterday (extend), two-day gap (reset to 1), and stored day in the future (treated as not-played, overwritten).
The daily win panel's primary button returns to the menu and never loads level N+1 (screenshot of the panel plus the resulting menu).
Losing the daily and pressing Retry regenerates a board with the same shape name and arrow count as the first attempt.
With `DAILY_ENABLED = false` the menu renders exactly as it does today (screenshot diff against the current build's menu).
steps.verification: (1) `npx jest src/ui/__tests__` for the SaveSystem daily-streak state machine with `SaveSystem.useClock` driving each transition — this covers the failing path (day-boundary arithmetic) rather than the component that happens to call it. (2) DEVICE, mandatory because this is UI: on the API 31 emulator capture a screenshot sequence — menu with 'Today's board', the daily board header showing the date, the daily win panel, and the menu afterwards still reading the same campaign level. (3) Day-rollover on device: `adb shell su 0 date` (or the emulator's date setting) forward one day, cold-start, screenshot the menu showing the daily available again and the streak incremented after a second clear. This is the only way to exercise the real rollover, since the injected clock in tests bypasses the device's own date handling.
steps.risk: Two real risks. (a) `registerDailySolve` touching `arrows_current_level` would silently skip a campaign level — guarded by an explicit unit assertion on currentLevel before/after. (b) A daily that takes far longer than a campaign Normal level would land the opposite of Naavik's constraint; W4-04 gates that claim, and `DAILY_ENABLED` is the rollback. Ship behind the flag; if W4-04's median comes back high, re-tune W4-03's band and re-derive its bounds rather than shipping the flag ON.
steps.brand_perf_check: FLAG TEST: PASSES — the daily adds no motion at all. It animates no arrow that is still in the static layer, adds no third concurrent exit trail (the 2-trail cap in exitAnimationConfig.ts:43, ArrowsBoardView.kt:391, ArrowsBoardView.swift:34 is untouched) and adds no fifth Skia feedback node (the pressed/blocker/shaking/hint set in StaticBoardSurface.native.tsx:175-220 is untouched). It reuses the existing board path wholesale. Brand gates: no second primary button (one violet accent preserved), no level-select grid, no timer, the board itself is unchanged and stays sacred.

steps.title: Make the day streak visible and forgiving (shields), instead of silently breaking to 0
steps.what:
TODAY'S BEHAVIOUR, read from the code: `SaveSystem.dayStreak` (saveSystem.ts:104-109) returns 0 the moment `today - last > 1`, and `registerSolve` (:122-126) then rewrites the stored streak to 1 — so the number is destroyed, not just hidden. It surfaces only inside `buildStatsLine` (HomeScreen.tsx:102-112) which appends it ONLY when `days >= 2`, into a single 13 pt `inkDim` line pinned to the bottom of the menu (styles.stats, HomeScreen.tsx:154-158). A player on a 1-day streak sees nothing; a player who misses one day loses everything with no message.

CHANGES. (a) SHIELDS: a new `arrows_streak_shields` int (0..2, from W4-01). On a solve after exactly a one-day gap, spend one shield and EXTEND the streak instead of resetting; on a gap of two or more days, reset regardless. Earn one shield per E consecutive days, capped at 2. E is escalated below — it is not measurable here and must not be invented. (b) READ HONESTLY: `dayStreak` currently returns 0 across a 1-day gap even before the next solve; change it to return the stored streak while a shield is available, so the menu does not flash a zero the player will not actually lose. (c) VISIBILITY: lift the streak out of the stats paragraph into its own element directly under the daily entry — `{n}-day streak` shown from 1 up, plus `· 1 saved` for a shield spend on the most recent gap. Keep it `inkDim`, keep the type in the brand family, and use no icon: no flame emoji, no badge, no new colour role. (The 💡 on the hint button is already an audited art gap; do not add a second emoji.) Leave the existing lifetime stats line intact for solved count and best perfect run.

NO ANIMATION in v1: DESIGN.md allows exactly one ambient motion on the menu (the Play pill's breathing, HomeScreen.tsx:48-58). A count-up on the streak number is a taste call, so it is escalated rather than assumed.
steps.why: Duolingo's finding is that raising the streak-freeze cap from 1 to 2-3 measurably improved return rates, i.e. forgiveness beats strictness; and JMIR 2023 (n=14,879, 899,071 sessions) found rigid daily temporal consistency predicted WORSE long-term persistence. Arrows currently ships the punishing version AND hides it — the strictest possible mechanic with none of the motivational payoff, which is the worst of both. Making it visible from 1 and survivable across one miss is the cheapest change in this workstream with real evidence behind it.
acceptance: Injected-clock state machine, all asserted: same-day solve (streak unchanged, no shield spent); next-day solve (streak +1, no shield); one-day gap with a shield (streak +1, shields -1, 'saved' flag set); one-day gap with no shield (streak resets to 1); two-day gap with two shields (streak resets to 1, no shields spent); shields never exceed 2 and never go below 0.
Menu shows '1-day streak' after a single solve on a fresh install (screenshot) — the current build shows nothing until 2.
Menu shows the preserved streak plus the saved indicator after a simulated one-day gap (screenshot with the device clock advanced by one day).
The existing lifetime stats line still renders solved count and best perfect run exactly as before (screenshot diff against the current build for a save with 400 solves).

Contrast: the streak element's text passes the same >=4.5:1 body target PRODUCT.md sets — `inkDim` on `bg` is documented at ~4.8:1 (Daylight) / ~6.5:1 (Ink Night) in DESIGN.md, so reuse that role and do not introduce a new colour.
steps.verification: (1) `npx jest src/core/__tests__/saveSystem.test.ts` driving every transition above through `SaveSystem.useClock` — this exercises the original failing behaviour because the bug is the reset arithmetic at saveSystem.ts:122-126, and the tests assert the stored streak value across each gap size, not merely that a getter returns a number. (2) DEVICE, mandatory (this is UI and this project has a scar from visual changes verified only by tsc): on the API 31 emulator, solve one level and screenshot the menu showing '1-day streak'; advance the emulator date by one day, solve again, screenshot showing '2-day streak'; advance by two days, solve, screenshot showing the reset. Three screenshots, attached to the PR.
steps.risk: The earn rate E is unmeasured and unmeasurable here (no analytics, no remote config, no A/B capability) — set too low it makes the streak meaningless, too high it never fires. Ship it as a single named constant `STREAK_SHIELD_EARN_DAYS` in saveSystem.ts so it is a one-line change, and record its value and rationale in project memory as a tunable, not a finding. Persistence risk: shields are a new key from W4-01, so a downgrade to versionCode 6 leaves them on disk untouched. Rollback: `STREAK_SHIELD_EARN_DAYS = Infinity` disables shields without touching the display change.
steps.brand_perf_check: FLAG TEST: PASSES — no motion is added at all in v1 (the count-up is escalated, not built), so no arrow is animated, no exit trail added, no Skia node added; the board is not touched. Brand gates: the menu keeps exactly one ambient motion (the Play pill), no emoji, no new colour role, no badge; 'calm, minimal' preserved. The one gate this brushes is DESIGN.md's spec that streak parts show 'only from 2 up' — this step deliberately changes that to 1 and DESIGN.md must be updated in the same commit rather than left contradicting the build.

steps.title: Shape collection: a gallery of the 26 silhouettes, with a cheap backfill for existing players
steps.what:
PERSISTENCE: a 26-bit set across `arrows_shapes_seen_lo` / `_hi` (30 bits each, 60 shapes of headroom) using `ShapeLibrary.catalogIndexOf` from W4-02. `SaveSystem.markShapeSeen(name)` sets the bit; `SaveSystem.shapesSeen(): boolean[]` reads it. Called from the win path in GameScreen.tsx (alongside the existing `SaveSystem.registerSolve` / `setCurrentLevel` calls at lines 121-122) and from the daily clear.

BACKFILL for existing players, run once inside W4-01's migration: for i in 0..currentLevel-1, set the bit for `shapeNameFor(i)` (W4-02). MEASURED cost: 2.17 ms per 1000 levels on this Mac under Node, versus 3211.6 ms per 1000 via full generation — the full-generation route is what makes a boot-time backfill impossible and the cheap lookup is what makes it trivial. Cap the loop at 5000 levels as a belt-and-braces bound and note that the dev-machine timing is NOT a Hermes-on-device timing: the acceptance criterion below is measured on the emulator, not inferred.

GALLERY: a new src/ui/CollectionScreen.tsx reached from a quiet menu entry. A grid of 26 tiles; each tile draws the shape by calling `ShapeDef.rasterize(14, Math.round(14 * aspect))` once at mount and folding the boolean mask into ONE `react-native-svg` `Path` per tile (memoized). Collected shapes render filled in `ink`; uncollected render as the same silhouette at low opacity in `border` — a dim ghost, not a '?' box, because the shapes ARE the content and teasing them is what makes it a collection. Shape name under each tile in the brand font. A count line: 'N of 26'. No level numbers, no tap-to-play, no navigation into a board — this is a gallery, not a level select.

No new dependency: react-native-svg 15.15.4 is already a direct dependency and already used in GameScreen.tsx for the heart pips.
steps.why: Audit finding: the 26 hand-authored silhouettes are the single richest collectible surface in the product and are discarded every level — they reach the player only as a token in a 12 pt subtitle (GameScreen.tsx:270). It is also the brand-compatible answer to the genre's arrow-skin convention, which PRODUCT.md ('no decorative colour soup') and DESIGN.md ('no per-arrow color') both forbid: the collectible is the picture the arrows drew, not a paint job on the arrows.
acceptance: Bit round-trip: setting each of the 26 catalog names individually and rehydrating from the two ints returns exactly that shape as seen and no other, for all 26 (unit test looping the catalog).

Bit positions are stable against the W4-02 order lock: a test asserts `catalogIndexOf('Square') === 0` etc. for the full 26, in the same file as the order-lock test, with a comment naming the save-format dependency.

Backfill correctness: for a save at currentLevel = 300, the backfilled set equals `new Set(range(0,300).map(shapeNameFor))` exactly — asserted against the full generator for a 300-level sample so the cheap lookup is not trusted on its own.

Backfill cost ON DEVICE: cold-start the app on the API 31 emulator with `arrows_current_level = 5000` seeded via adb, and measure boot-to-menu time against the same build with currentLevel = 0. Report both numbers and the delta. This must be measured, not extrapolated from the 2.17 ms/1000 dev-machine figure — Hermes is not Node.

Gallery renders all 26 tiles with distinct, recognisable silhouettes, with collected and uncollected states visually distinguishable, confirmed by an emulator screenshot in BOTH themes (the palette has six documented contrast failures, so the uncollected `border`-on-`bg` ghost must be checked by eye in Daylight, where `border` #E0DCEF on #FFFFFF is very faint).
Opening the gallery does not change the campaign resume level and offers no path into a board (screenshot of the screen plus its only exit control).
steps.verification: (1) `npx jest src/core/__tests__/saveSystem.test.ts` for the bitmask round-trip and the backfill-vs-full-generator equivalence — this exercises the real hazard (a bit position silently meaning a different shape) rather than asserting a setter set something. (2) DEVICE: emulator screenshots of the gallery in Daylight and Ink Night, one with a fresh save (all ghosts) and one with a backfilled 300-level save (mostly filled), attached to the PR. Component rendering cannot be verified in jest here — jest.config.js is node-env with `testMatch: **/src/**/__tests__/**/*.test.ts`, so no .tsx is testable in this repo today; the screenshots are the only evidence and must not be substituted with a passing unit suite. (3) The boot-time delta measurement above, run twice per configuration and reported with both runs.
steps.risk: (a) The catalog order is now save format; the W4-02 order-lock test plus the index assertions here are the guard, and both must be in the same file so a careless reorder cannot pass one and skip the other. (b) The backfill runs inside the migration, so a bug there runs on every existing player's first W4 launch — keep it strictly additive (it only ORs bits, never clears) and bounded at 5000 iterations. (c) 26 SVG paths on one screen is a new render cost on a screen that has never existed; the boot measurement above covers the migration, and the gallery itself must be screenshotted on the emulator before approval. Rollback: a `COLLECTION_ENABLED` flag hides the menu entry; the bits keep accruing harmlessly.
steps.brand_perf_check: FLAG TEST: PASSES — the gallery is a separate screen with no board on it. It animates no arrow in the static layer, adds no third concurrent exit trail, and adds no Skia feedback node (it uses react-native-svg, on a screen where the Skia overlay is not mounted). Tiles are static: no motion whatsoever. The per-solve `markShapeSeen` call is one int write on the already-existing win path, next to `registerSolve`. Brand gates: this is explicitly NOT a level-select grid (no level numbers, no entry into play) — the anti-reference is about navigating a grid every session, and this is an occasional gallery; it uses `ink` and `border` only, no new colour, no glow, no gradient, and it keeps direction-by-shape irrelevant since no arrows are drawn.

steps.title: Share artifact: a fixed-width text card of today's silhouette, no new dependency
steps.what:
CORRECTION TO A PREMISE, verified by reading the code: `makeImageSnapshotAsync` cannot capture the board. The Skia `Canvas` in src/ui/StaticBoardSurface.native.tsx:175-220 contains ONLY the four feedback nodes (pressed / blocker / shaking / hint); the arrows themselves live in the retained native view (modules/arrows-board). A snapshot of that canvas would return an essentially empty image. So an image card would have to be drawn from geometry into an offscreen Skia surface AND then handed to the OS, and delivering an image on Android needs a content:// URI, i.e. expo-sharing + expo-file-system, neither of which is installed. Image sharing is therefore out of scope for v1.

V1 IS TEXT, which is also what Wordle actually ships. Add a pure `buildDailyShareText(day, level, taps, hearts, streak)` in a new src/ui/shareCard.ts that renders `level.mask` (already on `GeneratedLevel`, levelGenerator.ts:16) cropped to its bounding box and downsampled to at most 12 columns, using ⬛ for a shape cell and ⬜ for a hole, plus a header line ('Arrows · <date>'), the shape name, taps, hearts remaining and the streak. React Native's core `Share.share({ message })` delivers it — no new dependency.

WHY EMOJI BLOCKS AND NOT ■: U+25A0 is not reliably fixed-width in the proportional fonts most chat clients use, so an ■ grid shears into a ragged blob — the grid only survives because emoji are rendered at a fixed advance. ⬛/⬜ keeps the card monochrome, so PRODUCT.md's 'no decorative colour soup' is respected while the grid still holds its shape. Cropping to the bounding box and using ⬜ only for interior holes keeps a typical card under ~180 characters.

ENTRY POINT: a plain 'Share' text button on the DAILY win panel only — not on campaign wins (there is nothing shared-in-common to compare), and not in the menu.

No URL in the message by default; a `SHARE_URL` constant the owner sets to the Play listing (escalated below, since an outbound marketing link is an owner decision).
steps.why: Wordle's emoji grid is the best-evidenced organic growth mechanism in daily puzzles, and it works precisely because everyone played the same board that day — which W4-03/05 now make true. It also costs nothing: no dependency, no asset, no server.
acceptance: For a known day, the emitted grid matches `generateDaily(day).mask` cropped and downsampled — asserted cell-by-cell against the mask, not against a golden string.
Every emitted card is <= 240 characters and <= 16 grid rows, across all 3650 days in the measured range (loop assertion, not a spot check).
Every grid row has the same number of grid glyphs (the property that makes it render as a shape).
No campaign win panel shows a Share button; the daily win panel does (two screenshots).
The card contains no personally identifying content and no level index — day, shape, taps, hearts, streak only.
Pasted into a real chat client on a phone, the silhouette is recognisable as the day's shape (see verification — this is the criterion the unit test cannot reach).
steps.verification: (1) `npx jest src/ui/__tests__/shareCard.test.ts` for the mask correspondence, the size ceiling over all 3650 days, and row-width uniformity — this exercises the failure that matters (a card whose grid does not correspond to the board, or which is truncated by a messaging client). (2) DEVICE, and this half is the one that actually closes it: on the API 31 emulator open the daily win panel, tap Share, screenshot the system share sheet, send the message to a real messaging client, and screenshot the received message. Pass = the shape is recognisable and no row is ragged. A unit test cannot verify glyph advance width in a third-party client's font, which is the specific risk this design is built around, so the pasted-message screenshot is mandatory evidence.
steps.risk: The whole design hinges on ⬛/⬜ rendering at a uniform advance in the recipient's client; the pasted-message screenshot is the check, and if it shears the fallback is a smaller grid (8 columns) or shape-name-only text. Downsampling a 40x40 mask to 12 columns can destroy thin silhouettes (Bolt, Crescent, Butterfly) — the acceptance loop should be eyeballed for those three specifically before approval. No persistence, no dependency, so rollback is hiding the button.
steps.brand_perf_check: FLAG TEST: PASSES — no motion, no animated arrow, no exit trail, no Skia node; the card is built once when the win panel is already up and the board is idle. Brand gates: monochrome by construction (⬛/⬜, no colour), no confetti, no glow; the emoji-square choice is a fixed-width necessity outside the app's own UI, and the app's own UI gains no emoji. It does bump against 'the board is sacred' only in the sense that it depicts the board — which is the point.

steps.title: One conditional local evening reminder (Android), asked in context and never on a played day
steps.what:
Add `expo-notifications` (not currently installed — verified against package.json and node_modules) and read https://docs.expo.dev/versions/v57.0.0/sdk/notifications/ before writing a line, per AGENTS.md. Add `android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS` to app.json's `android.permissions` (which today lists only `com.google.android.gms.permission.AD_ID`). Do NOT add SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM — a calm nudge does not need alarm-grade accuracy and Play scrutinises it.

PERMISSION IN CONTEXT: the request fires after the player's SECOND daily clear, from a one-line opt-in row on the daily win panel ('Remind me tomorrow evening?' with a plain yes / no-thanks). Never at first launch, never on the splash, never from the menu. Store the outcome in `arrows_notif_optin` (0 unasked / 1 granted / 2 declined) and never ask again once it is 2.

CADENCE — the part that needs care: expo-notifications' DAILY trigger fires unconditionally, which is 7 pushes a week, above the 2-5/week band where uninstall risk rises sharply, and gaming is the worst-performing vertical at under 1% CTR. So do not use a standing DAILY trigger as the whole design. Instead: on every app foreground and after every daily clear, cancel all scheduled notifications and schedule exactly ONE, for tomorrow at `arrows_notif_hour`, only if today's daily is already done; if the player has not opened the app for 3 consecutive days, cancel everything and schedule nothing until they return. Effective ceiling: at most one per day, at most 3 in a row without engagement.

Copy: one line, no urgency, no streak-loss threat ('Today's board is ready.'). Threatening a streak is exactly the rigid-consistency pattern JMIR 2023 associates with worse long-term persistence.

JS-TIMER SCAR APPLIES: the reschedule must run from an `AppState` listener (there are currently ZERO AppState usages in src/), not a JS timer — JS timers do not fire while Android has the app paused.
steps.why: The daily has no delivery channel; a daily board nobody is reminded of is a daily board only the already-retained player sees. Local scheduling needs no server and no FCM. The conditional design exists because the evidence on cadence is the strongest constraint in this step, not an afterthought.
acceptance: No permission dialog appears on first launch or before the second daily clear: a fresh install, played through one daily, shows no dialog (screen recording).
After a declined prompt the app never prompts again across at least three subsequent daily clears (`arrows_notif_optin === 2` and no dialog in the recording).
At most one notification is scheduled at any time: `getAllScheduledNotificationsAsync()` returns length <= 1 after each of — grant, daily clear, app foreground, three foregrounds in a row.
Nothing is scheduled for a day on which the daily has not been completed.
After three consecutive days without opening the app, nothing further is scheduled.
The manifest of the release build contains POST_NOTIFICATIONS and does NOT contain SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM (`aapt dump permissions` on the built APK).
Tapping the notification opens the app to the menu with today's daily available (recording).
steps.verification: (1) `aapt dump permissions` on the built release APK for the manifest assertions — this reads the artifact that Play actually reviews, not app.json. (2) EMULATOR: a scripted run that grants permission, clears a daily, foregrounds three times, and after each step logs `getAllScheduledNotificationsAsync()` — asserting the count and the trigger time, because the specific hazard is duplicate accumulating schedules from repeated foregrounds, and only enumerating the live schedule catches it. (3) A dev-only build path that schedules the reminder 45 seconds out instead of tomorrow, to observe an actual delivered notification and its tap-through on the emulator. (4) UNVERIFIABLE with today's tooling: real overnight delivery under Doze on a physical device, and the actual uninstall/CTR impact of the cadence. There is no physical device on any platform in this project and no analytics. Closing them needs one physical Android phone left overnight, and either analytics or a Play Console retention read.
steps.risk: Notifications are the highest-annoyance surface in the product and the failure mode (duplicate or nightly-regardless pings) directly causes uninstalls — the one thing this workstream is trying to prevent. Ship behind `NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED`, default OFF for the first release, and turn it on only after the emulator schedule-count evidence and one overnight physical-device run. Adding POST_NOTIFICATIONS also changes the Play listing's permission set, which is a release-time disclosure, not a silent change. Rollback: flag OFF plus `cancelAllScheduledNotificationsAsync()` on boot so already-scheduled reminders from a previous build are cleared.
steps.brand_perf_check: FLAG TEST: PASSES — no motion, no animated arrow, no exit trail, no Skia node. The AppState listener does no work on the gameplay path (it fires on foreground transitions, never during play). Brand gates: copy carries no urgency, no FOMO, no streak-loss threat — 'calm, night, minimal' extends to what the game says when it is closed. One notification per day at most is the quietest design that still has a delivery channel.

steps.title: Store review prompt at a perfect clear, quota-respecting and pre-gate-free
steps.what:
Add `expo-store-review` (not installed — verified against package.json) and read https://docs.expo.dev/versions/v57.0.0/sdk/storereview/ first per AGENTS.md. Trigger point: immediately after a PERFECT clear (no heart lost — the condition already computed at GameScreen.tsx:121 as `heartsRef.current === level.hearts`), which is Apple's stated 'moment of satisfaction'.

GATES, all AND-ed: `StoreReview.isAvailableAsync()` is true; `arrows_review_count < 3` (Apple's hard cap is 3 prompts per 365 days; 3 lifetime is stricter and simpler); `today - arrows_review_last_day >= 90` (Play's In-App Review API is quota-limited to roughly monthly and silently no-ops past it, so a 90-day self-gate keeps the app well inside both stores' budgets); and a minimum-engagement gate `SaveSystem.totalSolved >= N` (N escalated below — it is not derivable from anything measured, and this project's standing rule forbids inventing thresholds). On firing, write `arrows_review_last_day = today` and increment `arrows_review_count` REGARDLESS of what the OS does, because neither store tells the app whether a prompt was actually shown.

FORBIDDEN, explicitly: no 'Enjoying Arrows? 😊/😞' pre-gate (Play forbids it outright), no 'Rate us' button anywhere in the app (also forbidden by Play), no incentive of any kind, no prompt on a loss or on the daily's first-ever clear. The prompt must never block the win panel: call it after the panel is on screen and ignore the promise's result.
steps.why: Rating volume is the cheapest lever on store conversion, and the perfect clear is the only moment in this game that is unambiguously a satisfaction peak. It is specified tightly because both stores' rules here are prescriptive and the penalties (listing enforcement, silent no-ops that burn the quota) are invisible in testing.
acceptance: Gate logic unit-tested with the injected clock: fires on a perfect clear meeting all gates; does not fire on a non-perfect clear; does not fire on a loss; does not fire twice within 90 days; does not fire a fourth time ever; does not fire below the engagement threshold.

grep of src/ returns zero occurrences of a rate-us button, a satisfaction pre-gate, or any string like 'Enjoying' — asserted by a test that greps the UI sources, because this is a store-policy condition and a code-review eyeball is not a repeatable check.
On the API 31 emulator WITHOUT Play Services, a perfect clear produces no crash, no visible artefact, and the win panel remains fully interactive (screen recording).
`arrows_review_last_day` and `arrows_review_count` are written even when the OS shows nothing (asserted on the emulator run above by dumping the keys via adb afterwards).
steps.verification: (1) `npx jest src/core/__tests__/saveSystem.test.ts` for every gate combination with `SaveSystem.useClock` — this exercises the real hazard (burning the store's quota, or prompting a frustrated player) at the decision point rather than trusting the SDK call. (2) EMULATOR recording of a perfect clear on a Play-Services-free image, plus an `adb shell run-as` dump of the two keys afterwards, proving the bookkeeping happens even when the prompt is a no-op — that no-op path is the normal path in most test environments and is where silent bugs live. (3) UNVERIFIABLE here: whether the real dialog appears. `requestReview()` silently does nothing in TestFlight and is quota-throttled on Play. Closing it needs an internal-testing-track release on Play and someone watching a first-run device.
steps.risk: Low code risk, non-trivial policy risk: a pre-gate or a rate-us button is a listing-enforcement condition, which is why the grep assertion is a test and not a review note. Behavioural risk: prompting a player who is about to churn wastes one of three lifetime chances — that is what the engagement gate N is for, and N is escalated rather than guessed. Ship behind `REVIEW_PROMPT_ENABLED`; rollback is flag OFF, which leaves the counters untouched and costs nothing.
steps.brand_perf_check: FLAG TEST: PASSES — no motion, no animated arrow, no exit trail, no Skia node; the call is fired after the win panel has already rendered so it cannot land inside the clear animation's frames. Brand gates: no emoji pre-gate (also a store rule), no new UI surface at all, no menu entry — the calmest possible implementation is also the compliant one.

escalations.question: Should the daily board draw from all 26 shapes, or stay inside the Normal pool's four (Square / Rectangle / Circle / Diamond)?
escalations.options: (a) All 26 at Normal size — the daily shows a cat, a crown, a butterfly at 82 arrows. (b) Normal pool only — four shapes, so the daily is a plain filled rectangle roughly a quarter of the time. (c) All 26 but excluding Square and Rectangle, which have no picture at all.
escalations.recommendation: (a), or (c) if you want the daily to always be a picture. Measured over 3650 days at Normal config with the full catalog: median 82 arrows (p10 64, p90 100, mean 82.1), each shape appears 135-146 times against an expected 140, and only 4 of 3649 consecutive day-pairs repeat a shape. So (a) costs nothing in board size and buys near-uniform variety on the one board every player sees. (b) reproduces, on the daily, the exact audit finding that 33% of levels are a plain rectangle.
escalations.why_it_cannot_be_decided_here: It changes what the game's most visible board looks like every day — a brand and identity call, not a correctness one. It also mildly contradicts the existing tier convention that picture-book silhouettes are the SuperHard reward, and whether the daily gets to break that convention is yours.

escalations.question: What is the streak-shield earn rate (STREAK_SHIELD_EARN_DAYS), and should the cap be 2 or 3?
escalations.options: One shield per 5 / 7 / 10 consecutive days, capped at 2 or 3.
escalations.recommendation: One per 7 days, capped at 2. Duolingo's published result is that raising the cap from 1 to 2-3 improved returns; 7 days makes the reward legible ('a week buys you a miss') and the cap of 2 keeps a lapsed player from banking indefinite immunity. Be clear that 7 is a legibility choice, not a measured one.
escalations.why_it_cannot_be_decided_here: There is no analytics, no remote config and no A/B capability in this app, so no number here can be derived from this product's data — and the cited evidence constrains the CAP, not the earn rate. Any value I picked would be an unmeasured threshold in a brief, which is the exact failure this project has hit six times. Record whatever you choose in project memory as a tunable, not a finding.

escalations.question: What time should the evening reminder fire, and should it be evening at all?
escalations.options: 20:30 local / 19:00 local / a player-chosen hour / no time-of-day nudge at all (schedule nothing and rely on the daily existing).
escalations.recommendation: 20:30 local, fixed, with the hour stored in `arrows_notif_hour` so it is a one-line change. But note the tension honestly: PRODUCT.md positions this as a before-bed game, while the JMIR 2023 study (n=14,879, 899,071 sessions) found evening use decayed fastest and rigid daily consistency predicted worse long-term persistence. The evidence mildly argues against the positioning.
escalations.why_it_cannot_be_decided_here: It pits the product's own stated positioning against a cited external finding, with no way to test either in this app (no analytics). That trade is a positioning decision, not an engineering one.

escalations.question: How many lifetime solves before the store-review prompt is allowed to fire (N)?
escalations.options: N = 10 / 25 / 50, or 'first perfect clear after the third daily'.
escalations.recommendation: N = 25. It is not measured and I will not dress it as one: the only hard facts are Apple's cap of 3 prompts per year and Play's roughly monthly quota, neither of which constrains N. 25 solves is roughly two or three sessions of engagement, which keeps a first-session bounce from spending one of three lifetime chances.
escalations.why_it_cannot_be_decided_here: No telemetry exists to locate the engagement point where a player is likely to rate well, and the cost of a wrong N is invisible (a silently wasted prompt quota). It is a judgement call about how patient you want to be with a scarce, unobservable resource.

escalations.question: Should the share card carry a Play Store link, and should the grid be monochrome (⬛/⬜) or use the brand violet (🟪)?
escalations.options: (a) monochrome, no link; (b) monochrome, with the Play listing URL; (c) violet squares, with the link.
escalations.recommendation: (b). Monochrome holds PRODUCT.md's 'no decorative colour soup' line and still renders as a grid because emoji are fixed-width; the link is the entire growth mechanism, and a share card without one is a card that converts nobody. 🟪 would be more eye-catching and is what most Wordle clones do — it is a real trade, not a wrong answer.
escalations.why_it_cannot_be_decided_here: The card is outward-facing marketing that carries the brand into other people's chats, and the link makes it promotional. Both are owner decisions.

escalations.question: Should the menu streak number animate (a short count-up) when it increases?
escalations.options: (a) static text, ever; (b) a one-shot count-up when entering the menu after a solve that raised the streak.
escalations.recommendation: (a) for v1. DESIGN.md names exactly one deliberate ambient motion on the menu (the Play pill's breathing) and calls the menu calm; a count-up is defensible as feedback under design principle 4, but it is a taste call and the FLAG TEST cannot settle taste. If you want it, it must close on a screen recording, not on code review.
escalations.why_it_cannot_be_decided_here: Purely taste-based, on the surface the brand guards most explicitly. This project's rule is that visual/feel work closes on your eyeballs, not on math.

open_verification_gaps: MEASURED BY ME, ON THIS MAC UNDER NODE 20 — not on device, not under Hermes: `shapeNameFor` matches `LevelGenerator.generate().shapeName` for all levels 0-999 (0 mismatches) and costs 2.17 ms/1000 vs 3211.6 ms/1000 for full generation; the daily seed namespace has 0 collisions with campaign seeds over days 0-19999 x levels 0-199999; daily boards at Normal config with the 26-shape catalog run min 45 / p10 64 / median 82 / p90 100 / max 145 / mean 82.1 over 3650 days, with shapes appearing 135-146 times each and 4 consecutive-day repeats in 3649; campaign Normal levels run median 83 (p25 73, p75 93, n=400 over levels 0-599). Scripts are in the session scratchpad (m.ts, m2.ts, m3.ts, m4.ts) and MUST be committed under scripts/analysis/ or these numbers become unreproducible folklore.

TIME-TO-CLEAR IS UNMEASURED. Every claim that the daily is 'completable in a new player's first session' is UNVERIFIED until W4-04 runs. The 82-arrow median is a tap count, not a minute count, and the game is a visual-search task where tap count and time are only loosely related.

NO COMPONENT TESTS EXIST AND NONE CAN BE ADDED CHEAPLY. jest.config.js is node-env with `testMatch: **/src/**/__tests__/**/*.test.ts` — every .tsx in the project is untested and unreachable by the suite. Every UI acceptance criterion in W4-05, W4-06 and W4-07 therefore closes on an emulator screenshot and nothing else. Do not let a green jest run stand in for one.

NO PHYSICAL DEVICE, NO iOS. All verification lands on one API 31 Android emulator. The overnight notification delivery under Doze (W4-09), the store-review dialog actually appearing (W4-10), and the share card's glyph rendering in a real messaging client on a real phone (W4-08) are device-only and stay UNVERIFIED until one physical Android handset is in the loop.

THE ANDROID PERF HARNESS CANNOT VALIDATE ANY OF THIS. scripts/perf/android/benchmark.mjs sets animator_duration_scale=0, which flips Reanimated's useReducedMotion to true, and PERF_MODE boots straight into 'game' — so the menu, the splash, the collection screen and the daily entry are all unmeasurable by it. W4-07's boot-time backfill measurement must therefore be a manual cold-start timing, taken twice per configuration, not a harness run.

THE COLLECTION'S ON-DEVICE BACKFILL COST IS UNMEASURED. The 2.17 ms/1000 figure is Node on a Mac; Hermes on an emulator is a different instrument and the acceptance criterion in W4-07 is deliberately written as an emulator measurement rather than an extrapolation.

SHIELD EARN RATE, NOTIFICATION HOUR, AND THE REVIEW ENGAGEMENT THRESHOLD ARE UNMEASURABLE IN THIS PRODUCT — no analytics, no remote config, no A/B. They are escalated, not decided, and whatever values ship must be recorded in project memory as tunables so a later reader does not mistake them for findings.

REDUCE-MOTION AND THE AUDITED FEEDBACK BUG ARE UNTOUCHED HERE. W4 adds no motion, so it neither causes nor fixes the ReduceMotion.System defect at StaticBoardSurface.native.tsx:264/:308/:348 and BoardView.tsx:842/:887/:934 — but note that a reduce-motion player reaching the daily still gets no blocker flash and no hint pulse, so the daily's first-session claim is weaker for them than for anyone else until that workstream lands.

AUTO BACKUP IS ON AND UNDECLARED (allowBackup="true", no dataExtractionRules in the Android manifest). The eleven new keys from W4-01 will silently start syncing across a player's devices. W4-05 handles the one hazard I could identify (a restored `arrows_daily_day` in the future relative to the new device's clock); whether the collection and streak SHOULD travel across devices is a design question nobody has answered, and the backup configuration remains undeclared either way.
